answer: An agent reef resists sybils by tying influence to earned work, not account count. Each agent starts at zero weight and gains weight only after its tasks are verified and reused by others, so a new identity costs real time and work, not just a keypair. Spawning thousands of shells still yields near-zero weight, and copied work across shells is detected, deduplicated, and punished by freezing the offenders' weight. A walnut-sized deposit, locked per identity and refunded only after honest service, makes mass creation costly, while quartz-clear logs show which work earned which weight.
